items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Irving Randolph, the trumpet man known as "Mouse", came in to ask me to replace him at the Cafe Society Downtown

ctx.x: Al and I started rehearsing with Mary Lou Williams who had enjoyed the way we sounded when she replaced Ellis at the Cafe Society Uptown.

One day we were rehearsing at Mary Lou's apartment and Irving Randolph, the trumpet man known as "Mouse", came in to ask me to replace him at the Cafe Society Downtown where he was working with Edmond Hall, clarinetist. Mouse lived in the same building as Mary Lou and his wife was not feeling too well so he didn't want to leave her alone that night. I was not in a mood to want to play at the club that night and told Mouse that I didn't want to go back in that place again. Then I reconsidered and promised that I…

After the rehearsal and I was on my way home, I bought a pint of whisky, which I decided to take with me to the club. I had dinner in a restaurant and came home to change clothes. I opened my bottle and took a good taste from it and then put it in my trumpet case. Where I was living was a good 15 minutes walk to the 8th Avenue subway and when I came out to go to the gig, it was raining cats, dogs, and little fishes.
